blocks.title: Why Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning matters here

spans.text: Problem statement: A product team must choose whether labels, clusters, or rewards match a new AI feature. The learner's job is not to memorize Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning; it is to decide what to build or change, what evidence the system may use, and how to tell whether the change improved labels, clusters, or rewards match a new AI feature. They do not need trivia about Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning; they need a decision they can make, a concrete artifact they can inspect, and a way to know whether problem framed with the right feedback signal.

Running case: learning-paradigm decision guide for support and operations tasks. We will keep this same case through the lesson so each idea has a job: frame the problem, explain the mechanism, choose a design, test the implementation, and decide what to do next.

Before reading on, predict: if the team uses reinforcement learning where a labeled classifier would be simpler, where would you look first - the input, the state or data, the model boundary, the validation check, or the release process?

blocks.code:
# Supervised Unsupervised and Reinforcement Learning: tiny generalization diagnostic.
train_error = [0.04, 0.05, 0.05]
validation_error = [0.18, 0.19, 0.20]

def avg(xs):
    return sum(xs) / len(xs)

gap = avg(validation_error) - avg(train_error)
print(round(gap, 2))
print("do not ship" if gap > 0.10 else "continue")
